newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht weaker late, interbank rate rises.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht weaker late, interbank rate rises.

text.p: The Thai baht slipped against the dollar in late active trade on Wednesday as the U.S. unitcontinued to firm abroad, dealers said.
"The dollar/baht trade is very active today as U.S. unit's strength abroad prompted more dollar buying," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Buying of the dollar from the Bank of Thailand was also heavy today as the dollar had been traded very high in the interbank spot market against the central bank's fixing, dealers said.
The baht was traded at 25.905-25.915 to the dollar late compared with 25.890-25.895 earlier and 25.845-25.865 late on Tuesday, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar at 25.86, the lowest level in 6-1/2 years, against 25.81 on Tuesday.
"We may see the (baht/dollar) mid-rate being fixed at above 25.90 tomorrow. The dollar is very strong against the yen and mark," said another dealer.
Heavy buying of the dollar pushed the overnight interbank rate up to 11.75-12.00 percent late on Wednesday from 11.00-11.50 in the morning and 10.50-11.00 late on Tuesday, dealers said.
"Most local banks lent very small amount of funds to the market today. They maintained money to speculate in the rising dollar," said one money dealer at a European bank.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was at 9.50/10.00 satangs per dollar late, unchanged from early morning, dealers said.
